To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the provision of public goods by NGOs is an effective strategy in many contexts, but that there are also many risks.

(a) NGOs have been playing an increasing role in the provision of public goods in many developing countries; (b) NGOs are often more cost-effective than government agencies in delivering public goods and services; (c) NGOs are more effective in delivering public goods than private companies because NGOs have better incentives, better access to resources, better information and better accountability; (d) NGOs are often better at providing public goods and services to the poor; (e) NGOs have been successful in providing public goods
the role of NGOs in the public service delivery is important and that the government can play an important role in facilitating the process of service provision by NGOs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
three questions: (1) What are the conditions under which NGOs can provide effective public services?
the question of how to design public service delivery systems that are both efficient and equitable, and that can deliver services to the poor and the excluded.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the provision of public goods by the state, the market, and the third sector is not a zero-sum game.
NGOs are an important and useful complement to the state in the provision of public goods.
NGOs have the potential to improve public service delivery, but that the actual effectiveness of NGOs in providing public goods is contingent on a number of contextual factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single best way to provide public goods, and that a mix of different approaches, including those of NGOs, is needed.
the state is not a monopoly provider of public services.
NGOs can be effective providers of public goods in situations of weak state, but they are unlikely to be able to substitute for the state in situations where state is strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to rethink the way we think about public service delivery and to recognize the role of non-governmental organizations in this process.
the role of NGOs in public service delivery can be understood in a broader perspective than that of the traditional dichotomy of the state and the market.
the role of NGOs in public service provision can be a win-win situation for both the state and the citizens.
